copy.en: Sieves can have different sizes of holes, so you can choose the right sieve to separate fine sand from rocks or larger gravel from small pebbles.
copy.tl: Ang mga sieve ay maaaring magkaroon ng iba't ibang laki ng butas, kaya maaari mong piliin ang tamang sieve upang paghiwalayin ang pinong buhangin mula sa mga bato o ang mas malaking graba mula sa maliliit na bato.
copy.bis: Ang mga sieve mahimong adunay lainlaing gidak-on sa mga lungag, busa mahimo nimong pilion ang husto nga sieve aron bulagon ang pinong balas gikan sa mga bato o ang mas dako nga graba gikan sa gagmay nga mga bato.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The spinal cord serves as a channel for signals between the brain and most body parts
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss in small groups important concepts in the theories of evolution, such as variation, heredity, isolation, selection, and adaptation
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the function of the spinal cord in the nervous system. G10-L-4 is about discussing concepts in the theories of evolution (variation, heredity, isolation, selection, adaptation). There is no connection between spinal cord function and evolution concepts.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The spinal cord serves as a channel for signals between the brain and most body parts
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: differentiate sexual from asexual reproduction in terms of: a) number of parents involved, and b) similarities of offspring to parents
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the spinal cord's role in signal transmission and reflexes. G7-L-7 is about differentiating sexual from asexual reproduction. The card provides no information relevant to reproduction or the number of parents or offspring similarity.

copy.en: The spinal cord serves as a channel for signals between the brain and most body parts and controls some simple musculoskeletal reflexes without the brain's processing.
copy.tl: Ang spinal cord ay nagsisilbing channel para sa mga signal sa pagitan ng brain at karamihan ng bahagi ng katawan at kumokontrol sa ilang simpleng musculoskeletal reflexes kahit walang processing ng brain.
copy.bis: Ang spinal cord nagsilbi nga channel para sa mga signal tali sa brain ug sa daghang parte sa lawas ug nagkontrol sa pipila ka simple nga musculoskeletal reflexes bisan walay processing sa brain.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: High cholesterol silently builds up fat deposits in your blood vessels
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses high cholesterol and cardiovascular risk, which is unrelated to the solar system, celestial objects, or their composition. The assigned competency is about Earth and space science, so this tag is incorrect.

copy.en:
Why is high cholesterol dangerous if it has no symptoms?

High cholesterol silently builds up fat deposits in your blood vessels, which can later cause a heart attack or stroke.
copy.tl:
Bakit mapanganib ang high cholesterol kung wala itong sintomas?

Ang high cholesterol ay tahimik na nag-iipon ng mga fat deposits sa iyong mga ugat, na maaaring magdulot ng heart attack o stroke sa hinaharap.
copy.bis:
Ngano peligroso ang high cholesterol kung wala kini sintomas?

Ang high cholesterol hilom nga magtigom ug mga fat deposits sa imong mga ugat, nga mahimong magpahinabo ug heart attack o stroke sa umaabot.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You can throw trash in the proper bin, join clean-up activities, and use eco-bags

assignedReviews.reason: The card is about simple environmental protection actions (proper trash disposal, clean-ups, eco-bags). It contains no information about subatomic particles, their symbols, mass, charge, or location within an atom.

assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses environmental actions and has nothing to do with drawing the structure of an atom, nucleus, or electron shells.

copy.en:
What simple actions can I do to protect the environment?

You can throw trash in the proper bin, join clean-up activities, and use eco-bags, because small actions add up to keep the environment healthy!
copy.tl:
Anong mga simpleng gawain ang maaari kong gawin upang maprotektahan ang kapaligiran?

Maaari kang magtapon ng basura sa tamang basurahan, sumali sa mga clean-up activity, at gumamit ng eco-bag, dahil ang maliliit na gawain ay sama-samang nakakatulong upang mapanatiling malusog ang kapaligiran!
copy.bis:
Unsa nga mga simple nga buhat ang akong mahimo aron mapanalipdan ang kalikopan?

Mahimo kang maglabay ug basura sa husto nga basurahan, moapil sa mga clean-up activity, ug mogamit ug eco-bag, tungod kay ang gagmay nga mga buhat magdungan ug makatabang aron magpabiling himsog ang kalikopan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A simple microscope uses only one lens to magnify objects
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe examples and uses of simple machines found at home, at school, and in the community
assignedReviews.reason: A simple microscope is an optical instrument, not a simple machine. Simple machines are devices like levers, pulleys, inclined planes, wedges, screws, and wheels and axles. The card does not describe any simple machine or its use, so it does not support G6-F-1.

copy.en: A simple microscope uses only one lens to magnify objects, like the lens in a jewelry eyepiece or a reading glass.
copy.tl: Ang simple microscope ay gumagamit lamang ng isang lens para palakihin ang mga bagay, tulad ng lens sa jewelry eyepiece o reading glass.
copy.bis: Ang simple microscope naggamit ug usa ra ka lens aron padak-on ang mga butang, sama sa lens sa jewelry eyepiece o reading glass.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Objects can be compared by size and volume

assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches comparing objects by size and volume (using dalandan vs kalamansi), which is unrelated to the competency about demonstrating factors affecting solubility of a solute in a solvent, such as heat. No solubility content is present.

copy.en: Objects can be compared by size and volume, like a dalandan being bigger and having more volume than a kalamansi.
copy.tl: Maaaring paghambingin ang mga bagay ayon sa laki at volume, tulad ng dalandan na mas malaki at mas marami ang volume kaysa sa kalamansi.
copy.bis: Ang mga butang mahimong ikumpara pinaagi sa gidak-on ug volume, sama sa dalandan nga mas dako ug mas daghan ang volume kaysa sa kalamansi.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Activities like skating need less friction
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: investigate and describe the relationship among the projectile variables including the angle and velocity of release, and projectile height and range, using everyday activities such as shooting basketballs or kicking footballs
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses friction and skating, which is unrelated to projectile motion variables (angle, velocity, height, range). It does not support the competency's content.

copy.en: Activities like skating need less friction so that the skates can glide smoothly and quickly over the ice or floor.
copy.tl: Ang mga gawain tulad ng skating ay nangangailangan ng mas kaunting friction upang ang mga skate ay makadausdos nang maayos at mabilis sa yelo o sahig.
copy.bis: Ang mga buluhaton sama sa skating nagkinahanglan og mas gamay nga friction aron ang mga skate makadaus-os og hapsay ug paspas sa yelo o salog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The outer epidermis is a tough shield facing the world, and the inner dermis holds blood vessels, glands, and nerves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The competency G4-L-1 specifically requires describing how the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory systems work. The card describes the skin's layers (epidermis and dermis), which is the integumentary system and is not one of the listed systems. It provides no instructional support for any of the five required systems.

copy.en:
What are the two main layers of skin?

The outer epidermis is a tough shield facing the world, and the inner dermis holds blood vessels, glands, and nerves — together protecting what's inside your body.
copy.tl:
Ano ang dalawang pangunahing kapa ng balat?

Ang epidermis sa labas ay matibay na takip laban sa panlabas, at ang dermis sa loob ay may mga ugat, glands, at nerves — magkasama nilang pinoprotektahan ang loob ng katawan.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang duha ka nag-unang kapa sa panit?

Ang epidermis sa gawas mao ang gahi nga taklob batok sa kalibutan, ug ang dermis sa sulod naay mga ugat, glands, ug nerves — magkuyog nga naga-panalipod sa sulod sa lawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The skin acts as a receptor for touch, pressure, pain, heat, and cold

assignedReviews.reason: Card is about skin sensory receptors, completely unrelated to subduction of oceanic plates.

assignedReviews.reason: Card is about skin sensory receptors, unrelated to Philippine Archipelago map or plate tectonics.

copy.en: The skin acts as a receptor for touch, pressure, pain, heat, and cold, sending messages to the brain about the outside world.
copy.tl: Ang balat ay nagsisilbing receptor para sa touch, pressure, pain, heat, at cold—nagpapadala ito ng mensahe sa utak tungkol sa labas na mundo.
copy.bis: Ang panit nagsilbing receptor alang sa touch, pressure, pain, heat, ug cold—magpadala kini ug mensahe sa utok mahitungod sa gawas nga kalibutan.

assignedReviews.reason: The card is about weather observation, not about structures, movements, or events at plate boundaries.

assignedReviews.reason: The card contains nothing about tectonic plate movement mechanisms or the asthenosphere; it is unrelated to plate tectonics.

copy.en: Sky condition is one way to describe weather by looking at what covers the sky, such as sunshine, clouds, or rain.
copy.tl: Ang sky condition ay isang paraan upang ilarawan ang panahon sa pamamagitan ng pagtingin sa kung ano ang nasa langit, tulad ng sikat ng araw, ulap, o ulan.
copy.bis: Ang sky condition usa ka paagi sa paghulagway sa panahon pinaagi sa pagtan-aw kung unsa ang naa sa langit, sama sa kahayag sa adlaw, panganod, o ulan.

assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses sleep duration by age, not life-cycle stages of animals, and does not use a flow chart as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.reason: The card is about sleep needs across human ages, not about comparing life cycles of mammals, birds, or plants from birth/egg/seed to maturity.

copy.en: How much sleep you need changes with age — babies sleep the longest, school kids need about 9 to 12 hours, and adults need only about 7 to 8. The younger you are, the more sleep you need!
copy.tl: Nagbabago ang kailangang tulog ayon sa edad — pinakamahaba ang tulog ng sanggol, ang batang nag-aaral ay mga 9 hanggang 12 oras, at ang matanda ay mga 7 hanggang 8 oras lang. Mas bata, mas mahaba ang tulog!
copy.bis: Ang gikinahanglan nga tulog mausab sumala sa edad — pinakataas ang tulog sa masuso, ang batang nag-eskwela mga 9 ngadto 12 ka oras, ug ang tigulang mga 7 ngadto 8 lang ka oras. Kon mas bata, mas taas ang tulog!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: you pass through different stages each night, from light sleep to deep sleep
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes stages of sleep, which is not part of the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, or respiratory systems. It does not support the competency at all.

copy.en: Sleep isn't just one thing — you pass through different stages each night, from light sleep to deep sleep.
copy.tl: Hindi iisa lang ang tulog — dumadaan ka sa iba't ibang yugto tuwing gabi, mula sa mababaw hanggang sa mahimbing na tulog.
copy.bis: Dili usa ra ka klase ang tulog — moagi ka sa lain-laing bahin matag gabii, gikan sa mabaw hangtod sa lawom nga tulog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It tells us how steep the line is, which is the rise over the run, or the change in y divided by the change in x.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain properties of metals in terms of their structure and metallic bonding (sea of electrons model)
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the slope of a line on a motion graph (rise over run, change in y over change in x). This is a mathematics/physics concept about graphs, completely unrelated to the competency, which requires explaining properties of metals in terms of their structure and metallic bonding (sea of electrons model).

copy.en:
What does the slope of a line on a motion graph tell us?

It tells us how steep the line is, which is the rise over the run, or the change in y divided by the change in x.
copy.tl:
Ano ang sinasabi ng slope ng isang linya sa motion graph?

Sinasabi nito kung gaano katarik ang linya, na ang ibig sabihin ay rise over run, o ang pagbabago sa y na hinati sa pagbabago sa x.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang gisulti sa slope sa usa ka linya sa motion graph?

Kini nagsulti kung unsa ka titip ang linya, nga mao ang rise over run, o ang pagbag-o sa y nga gibahin sa pagbag-o sa x.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Smell and taste are special partners
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models or illustrations to explain how movements along faults generate earthquakes and identify and explain which types of faults are most likely to occur in the Philippines and explain why
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses how smell and taste work together to perceive flavor, which is unrelated to the competency about using models or illustrations to explain how movements along faults generate earthquakes and identifying fault types in the Philippines.

copy.en: Smell and taste are special partners, working together so we can enjoy the full flavor of our food.
copy.tl: Ang pang-amoy at panlasa ay espesyal na magkapareha, na nagtutulungan upang maramdaman natin ang buong lasa ng ating pagkain.
copy.bis: Ang pagpanimaho ug pagtilaw espesyal nga magkauban, nga nagtinabangay aron atong mabati ang tibuok lami sa atong pagkaon.

assignedReviews.reason: The card describes smoke as a gas and particle movement, but does not mention heat energy or any change of state process. It provides no instructional support for the role of heat energy in melting, evaporation, freezing, or condensation.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe any change of state (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation) nor use diagrams or flowcharts. It only states that smoke is a gas with freely moving molecules, which is unrelated to the competency's focus on state changes.

copy.en: Smoke is a gas made of tiny particles floating in the air, and it spreads out quickly because its molecules move freely.
copy.tl: Ang usok ay gas na binubuo ng maliliit na particle na lumulutang sa hangin, at mabilis itong kumakalat dahil malayang gumagalaw ang mga molecule nito.
copy.bis: Ang aso usa ka gas nga gilangkuban sa gagmay nga mga particle nga naglutaw sa hangin, ug dali kini nga mokatap tungod kay ang mga molecule niini gawasnon nga molihok.

assignedReviews.reason: The card is about air pollution and global warming, not about describing living things as biotic factors or light, water, temperature, and soil type as abiotic factors in an ecosystem. It does not support the competency's content.

copy.en: Smoke and toxins from burning materials enter the air and contribute to global warming, the gradual heating of the Earth.
copy.tl: Ang usok at mga lason mula sa nasusunog na materyales ay pumapasok sa hangin at nag-aambag sa global warming, ang unti-unting pag-init ng mundo.
copy.bis: Ang aso ug mga hilo nga nagagikan sa nagdilaab nga materyales mosulod sa hangin ug makatampo sa global warming, ang hinay-hinay nga pag-init sa kalibotan.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce); it is about smoking's harmful effects on the body.

copy.en: Cigarette smoking harms nearly every organ in the human body, causing many illnesses and affecting overall health.
copy.tl: Ang paninigarilyo ay nakakasira sa halos bawat organ sa katawan ng tao, na nagdudulot ng maraming sakit at nakakaapekto sa pangkalahatang kalusugan.
copy.bis: Ang pagpanigarilyo makadaot sa halos matag organ sa lawas sa tao, nga hinungdan sa daghang mga sakit ug makaapekto sa kinatibuk-ang panglawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Rubbing loosens stuck germs and dirt
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate various techniques in separating mixtures, such as decantation, winnowing, scooping, picking, evaporation, filtering, sieving, and using magnets
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains how rubbing and soap remove dirt and germs during handwashing. It does not demonstrate any mixture separation technique (decantation, winnowing, scooping, picking, evaporation, filtering, sieving, magnets) and is unrelated to the competency.

copy.en:
Is smearing soap on your hands enough to get clean?

Not quite! Rubbing loosens stuck germs and dirt, while soap wraps them so they can't stick back. Soap and scrubbing work as a team!
copy.tl:
Sapat na ba na ipahid lang ang sabon para maging malinis?

Hindi pa! Kinakuskos ang nakakapit na germ at dumi, at binabalot ng sabon para hindi bumalik. Magkatulong ang sabon at kuskos!
copy.bis:
Igo na ba nga ipahid lang ang sabon aron maglimpyo?

Dili pa! Ang pagkuskos magluag sa nipilit nga germ ug hugaw, ug putoson sa sabon aron dili mobalik. Magtinabangay ang sabon ug kuskos!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Soap molecules trap tiny air pockets inside thin water films to make bubbles!

assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why soap produces bubbles and lather, focusing on soap molecules, air pockets, and water films. copy.en: Soap molecules trap tiny air pockets inside thin water films to make bubbles! That’s why rubbing soap creates thick, foamy lather.
copy.tl: Ang mga molekula ng sabon ay bumabalot sa maliliit na hangin sa loob ng manipis na tubig para gumawa ng bula! Kaya kapag kinusot mo, lumalabas ang makapal na lather.
copy.bis: Ang mga molekula sa sabon mobalot sa gagmay nga hangin sulod sa nipis nga tubig para mohimo og bula! Mao nga kung kuso-kusoon nimo, mogawas ang baga nga lather.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The water-loving end of soap is called the head! It holds tightly onto water.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe that particles are constantly in motion, have spaces between them, attract each other, and move faster as the temperature increases (or with the addition of heat)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the hydrophilic head of soap and its attraction to water. It does not address particle motion, spacing, attraction between particles, or temperature effects, which are the core of G7-M-3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The water-loving end of soap is called the head! It holds tightly onto water.

assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a property of soap molecules (hydrophilic head) but does not describe the Particle Model of Matter, which states that all matter is made of tiny particles with each pure substance having its own kind of particles. No particle-level explanation is given.

copy.en: The water-loving end of soap is called the head! It holds tightly onto water.
copy.tl: Ang dulong mahilig sa tubig ay tinatawag na ulo ng sabon! Ito ang humahawak sa tubig.
copy.bis: Ang tumoy sa sabon nga ganahan sa tubig gitawag nga ulo! Kini ang mokupot sa tubig.

What is the empirical formula of a compound with sodium, aluminum, and fluorine?

Ano ang empirical formula ng isang compound na may sodium, aluminum, at fluorine?

Sa 32.79% Na, 13.02% Al, at 54.19% F, ang empirical formula ay Na3AlF6, isang mineral na tinatawag na cryolite!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang empirical formula sa usa ka compound nga adunay sodium, aluminum, ug fluorine?

Sa 32.79% Na, 13.02% Al, ug 54.19% F, ang empirical formula mao ang Na3AlF6, usa ka mineral nga gitawag og cryolite!

copy.bis: Ang sodium nitrate (NaNO3) kay 27.05% sodium, 16.48% nitrogen, ug 56.47% oxygen pinaagi sa gibug-aton.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mollusks like snails and octopuses have soft bodies
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: distinguish among comets, meteoroids, asteroids, and dwarf planets, and describe how they help us to understand the nature and formation of the Earth and the Solar System
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes mollusks (soft-bodied animals), which is unrelated to distinguishing comets, meteoroids, asteroids, and dwarf planets or understanding the formation of the Solar System.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mollusks like snails and octopuses have soft bodies
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about mollusks, not the general structure of the solar system or major celestial objects. No connection to the competency.

copy.en: Mollusks like snails and octopuses have soft bodies, and some have shells or tentacles on their heads.
copy.tl: Ang mga mollusk tulad ng kuhol at octopus ay may malalambot na katawan, at ang ilan ay may mga shell o tentacle sa kanilang mga ulo.
copy.bis: Ang mga mollusk sama sa kuhol ug octopus adunay humok nga mga lawas, ug ang uban adunay mga shell o tentacle sa ilang mga ulo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Pick a toothbrush with soft bristles and brush gently
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about dental hygiene (soft bristles protect gums), not about describing how the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, or respiratory systems work. It does not support the competency.

copy.en: Pick a toothbrush with soft bristles and brush gently — it keeps your gums safe from getting hurt.
copy.tl: Pumili ng sipilyong may malambot na bristle at magsipilyo nang marahan — para hindi masaktan ang gilagid mo.
copy.bis: Pagpili og sepilyo nga humok ang bristle ug sepilyoha nga hinay-hinay — aron dili masakitan ang imong lagus.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Edaphic factors like the shape of the land and the minerals in the soil decide which plants can live there!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Edaphic factors like the shape of the land and the minerals in the soil decide which plants can live there!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about edaphic factors and plant growth, not about how temperature changes cause matter to change state. No instructional support for this competency.

copy.en:
Why do different plants grow on a mountain than in a valley?

Edaphic factors like the shape of the land and the minerals in the soil decide which plants can live there!
copy.tl:
Bakit iba ang mga halaman sa bundok kaysa sa lambak?

Ang edaphic factors tulad ng hugis ng lupa at mga mineral sa lupa ang nagdedesisyon kung aling mga halaman ang maaaring tumira doon!
copy.bis:
Ngano lahi man ang mga tanom sa bukid kaysa sa walog?

Ang edaphic factors sama sa porma sa yuta ug mga mineral sa yuta ang nagdesisyon kon unsang mga tanom ang mabuhi didto!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Soil conservation methods like strip-cropping, contour farming, and terracing reduce erosion
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: distinguish among comets, meteoroids, asteroids, and dwarf planets, and describe how they help us to understand the nature and formation of the Earth and the Solar System
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about soil conservation and erosion control; it contains no information about comets, meteoroids, asteroids, dwarf planets, or the formation of the Earth and Solar System.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Soil conservation methods like strip-cropping, contour farming, and terracing reduce erosion
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses soil conservation and erosion, not the general structure of the solar system, celestial objects, or their features and composition.

copy.en: Soil conservation methods like strip-cropping, contour farming, and terracing reduce erosion by slowing down water runoff and keeping the nutrient-rich topsoil in place.
copy.tl: Ang mga paraan ng soil conservation tulad ng strip-cropping, contour farming, at terracing ay nagbabawas ng erosion sa pamamagitan ng pagpapabagal ng daloy ng tubig at pagpapanatili ng masustansyang topsoil sa lugar nito.
copy.bis: Ang mga pamaagi sa soil conservation sama sa strip-cropping, contour farming, ug terracing makapamenos sa erosion pinaagi sa pagpahinay sa pag-agos sa tubig ug pagpabilin sa sustansiyadong topsoil sa iyang nahimutangan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Soil is arranged in layers called horizons
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the formation of ions as either the loss or gain of electrons to produce ionic bonds, using examples, such as the formation of sodium chloride
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes soil horizons and a soil profile, which is earth science content. It provides no information about ion formation, electron loss/gain, or ionic bonds, so it does not support G9-M-5.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Soil is arranged in layers called horizons
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: write the chemical formula and chemical names of some common ionic compounds, including sodium chloride (NaCl), magnesium oxide (MgO), potassium chloride (KCl) and magnesium chloride (MgCl2)
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about soil layers, not chemical formulas or names of ionic compounds. It does not support G9-M-6.

copy.en: Soil is arranged in layers called horizons, and these layers together form a soil profile.
copy.tl: Ang lupa ay nakaayos sa mga patong na tinatawag na horizons, at ang mga patong na ito ay bumubuo ng soil profile.
copy.bis: Ang yuta gihan-ay sa mga patong nga gitawag ug horizons, ug kining mga patong nagporma ug soil profile.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Soil plays a role in climate regulation through carbon sequestration, which means it stores carbon from the air in the ground.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of pure substances as: a. having fixed chemical composition, examples of which are elements and compounds, and b. that all the atoms of an element have a unique number of protons
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses carbon sequestration by soil and climate regulation. It does not address pure substances, fixed chemical composition, elements/compounds, or unique proton numbers, so it provides no instructional support for this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Soil plays a role in climate regulation through carbon sequestration, which means it stores carbon from the air in the ground.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the Particle Model of Matter as 'All matter is made up of tiny particles with each pure substance having its own kind of particles.'
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about soil storing carbon and climate regulation. It does not describe the Particle Model of Matter, particles, or pure substances having their own kind of particles, so it is unrelated to this competency.

copy.en: Soil plays a role in climate regulation through carbon sequestration, which means it stores carbon from the air in the ground.
copy.tl: Ang lupa ay may papel sa climate regulation sa pamamagitan ng carbon sequestration, ibig sabihin iniimbak nito ang carbon mula sa hangin sa ilalim ng lupa.
copy.bis: Ang yuta adunay papel sa climate regulation pinaagi sa carbon sequestration, buot ipasabot gitipigan niya ang carbon nga naggikan sa hangin sa ilalom sa yuta.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In a solar eclipse model
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify examples of everyday situations that demonstrate: a. kinetic energy being transformed to potential energy, and b. potential energy being transformed to kinetic energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a solar eclipse model (flashlight as Sun, circles as Moon and Earth), which is an astronomy/space-science topic. G8-F-5 requires identifying everyday situations demonstrating kinetic-to-potential or potential-to-kinetic energy transformations. The card provides no information about energy transformations, so the tag is unrelated.

copy.en: In a solar eclipse model, a flashlight represents the Sun, a small circle represents the Moon, and a bigger circle represents Earth, all aligned in a row.
copy.tl: Sa model ng solar eclipse, ang flashlight ay kumakatawan sa Araw, ang maliit na bilog ay kumakatawan sa Buwan, at ang mas malaking bilog ay kumakatawan sa Earth, lahat nakapila nang tuwid.
copy.bis: Sa model sa solar eclipse, ang flashlight nagrepresentar sa Adlaw, ang gamay nga lingin nagrepresentar sa Bulan, ug ang mas dako nga lingin nagrepresentar sa Earth, tanang naglinya og tarong.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Solids can have different shapes, including round, square, rectangle, triangle, and oblong.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes shapes of solids, which is a matter/physics topic. G4-L-3 requires classifying Philippine animals and plants by habitat using a drawing or diagram. There is no connection to living things, habitats, or classification.

copy.en: Solids can have different shapes, including round, square, rectangle, triangle, and oblong.
copy.tl: Ang mga solid ay maaaring magkaroon ng iba't ibang hugis, tulad ng bilog, parisukat, parihaba, tatsulok, at oblong.
copy.bis: Ang mga solid mahimong adunay lain-laing porma, sama sa lingin, kwadrado, rektanggulo, triyanggulo, ug oblong.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Covalent compounds are usually insoluble in water but soluble in organic solvents like alcohol or oil.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: measure accurately the distance and time when things move using simple equipment
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses solubility of covalent compounds, a chemistry topic. G4-F-2 requires measuring distance and time when things move, which is unrelated to solubility.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Covalent compounds are usually insoluble in water but soluble in organic solvents like alcohol or oil.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that forces act between objects and can be measured
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses solubility of covalent compounds, a chemistry topic. G7-F-1 requires identifying that forces act between objects and can be measured, which is unrelated to solubility.

copy.en: Covalent compounds are usually insoluble in water but soluble in organic solvents like alcohol or oil.
copy.tl: Ang mga covalent compound ay kadalasang hindi natutunaw sa tubig pero natutunaw sa organic solvents tulad ng alcohol o oil.
copy.bis: Ang mga covalent compound kasagarang dili matunaw sa tubig apan matunaw sa organic solvents sama sa alcohol o oil.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Whether a solute dissolves in a solvent depends on the nature of both substances
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain properties of metals in terms of their structure and metallic bonding (sea of electrons model)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses solubility based on the nature of solute and solvent, which is a physical dissolution concept. G9-M-10 requires explaining properties of metals in terms of metallic bonding and the sea of electrons model. The card contains no information about metals, metallic structure, or bonding, so it does not support the competency at all.

copy.en: Whether a solute dissolves in a solvent depends on the nature of both substances, because similar particles tend to mix well together.
copy.tl: Kung matutunaw ba ang isang solute sa solvent ay nakadepende sa kalikasan ng dalawang substance, dahil ang magkatulad na particle ay madaling maghalo.
copy.bis: Kung matunaw ba ang usa ka solute sa solvent nagdepende sa kinaiyahan sa duha ka substance, tungod kay ang parehas nga particle dali nga magsagol.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A good mitigation plan proposes solutions
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use weather instruments to measure and record some of the characteristics of weather during a school day
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses mitigation plans and matching solutions to negative impacts (e.g., replanting trees). It has no connection to using weather instruments to measure and record weather characteristics during a school day.

copy.en: A good mitigation plan proposes solutions that directly fix the specific negative impacts identified, like planting new trees where forests were cut down.
copy.tl: Ang isang mahusay na mitigation plan ay nagmumungkahi ng mga solusyon na direktang umaayos sa mga natukoy na negatibong epekto, tulad ng pagtatanim ng mga bagong puno kung saan pinutol ang mga kagubatan.
copy.bis: Ang usa ka maayong mitigation plan nagsugyot og mga solusyon nga direktang nag-ayo sa mga nailhan nga negatibong epekto, sama sa pagtanom og bag-ong mga kahoy diin giputol ang mga kalasangan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Q = I × t = 10 A × 120 s = 1200 coulombs
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches calculating electric charge from current and time, which is a physics/electricity concept. G5-E-11 is about describing the general structure of the solar system, celestial objects, and their composition. There is no overlap in subject matter.

copy.en: If a current of 10 amperes flows for 120 seconds, the charge that moves is Q = I × t = 10 A × 120 s = 1200 coulombs.
copy.tl: Kung ang current na 10 amperes ay dumaloy sa loob ng 120 segundo, ang charge na gumalaw ay Q = I × t = 10 A × 120 s = 1200 coulombs.
copy.bis: Kung ang current nga 10 amperes moagos sa 120 ka segundo, ang charge nga milihok kay Q = I × t = 10 A × 120 s = 1200 coulombs.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Add their momenta before the collision
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how soil is formed from rocks and minerals
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches how to compute the shared velocity of two sticking billiard balls using momentum, a physics topic. It has no relation to soil formation from rocks and minerals.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Add their momenta before the collision
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in a guided investigation to identify the effect of different types of soil on the growth of plants
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about momentum and collisions, not about the effect of different soil types on plant growth.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Add their momenta before the collision
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities using simple equipment to compare different types of soil including sandy, clay, silt, and loam, including comparing the ability of the soils to hold water
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about momentum and collisions, not about comparing soil types or their water-holding ability.

copy.en:
How do you find the speed of two billiard balls that stick together after colliding?

Add their momenta before the collision, then divide by their combined mass to get the new shared velocity!
copy.tl:
Paano mo makukuha ang bilis ng dalawang billiard balls na magkadikit pagkatapos magbanggaan?

Idagdag ang kanilang momenta bago magbanggaan, pagkatapos hatiin sa pinagsamang mass nila para makuha ang bagong magkasamang velocity!
copy.bis:
Unsaon nimo pagkuha ang kapaspas sa duha ka billiard balls nga magtapot pagkahuman sa bangga?

Idugang ang ilang momenta sa wala pa ang bangga, dayon bahina sa ilang gikombinar nga mass aron makuha ang bag-ong gipaambit nga velocity!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sound can be a signal that carries information
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that the arrangement of elements in the periodic table as 7 periods and 18 groups is based on their atomic structure and chemical properties, such as reactivity
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains that sound can carry information as a signal (whistle, drumbeat, bell). It has no connection to the periodic table arrangement, periods, groups, atomic structure, or chemical properties.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sound can be a signal that carries information
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of pure substances as: a. having fixed chemical composition, examples of which are elements and compounds, and b. that all the atoms of an element have a unique number of protons
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about sound as a signal, not about pure substances, fixed chemical composition, elements, compounds, or protons. The assigned competency is entirely unrelated to the card content.

copy.en: Sound can be a signal that carries information, like a whistle telling players to stop, a drumbeat calling people together, or a bell announcing that class is over.
copy.tl: Ang tunog ay maaaring maging signal na may dalang impormasyon, tulad ng whistle na nagsasabi sa mga manlalaro na huminto, isang drumbeat na tumatawag sa mga tao, o isang bell na nag-aanunsyo na tapos na ang klase.
copy.bis: Ang tingog mahimong usa ka signal nga nagdala og impormasyon, sama sa whistle nga nagsulti sa mga magdudula nga mohunong, usa ka drumbeat nga nagtawag sa mga tawo, o usa ka bell nga nag-anunsyo nga humana na ang klase.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sound energy is produced by vibrating objects
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate through guided investigation the advantages and limitations of simple machines, such as inclined planes, wedges, levers, and pulleys
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines sound energy and sound waves; it does not address simple machines, inclined planes, wedges, levers, or pulleys, nor any guided investigation of their advantages and limitations.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sound energy is produced by vibrating objects
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe examples and uses of simple machines found at home, at school, and in the community
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about sound energy and sound waves, not about observing or describing examples and uses of simple machines at home, school, or community.

copy.en: Sound energy is produced by vibrating objects or bodies, and these vibrations create sound waves that travel through a medium.
copy.tl: Ang sound energy ay nagagawa ng mga vibrating objects o katawan, at ang vibrations na ito ay lumilikha ng sound waves na naglalakbay sa pamamagitan ng medium.
copy.bis: Ang sound energy mugna sa mga vibrating objects o lawas, ug kini nga vibrations naghimo ug sound waves nga mobiyahe pinaagi sa medium.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: People use sound energy to communicate
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to explain how potential energy stored in lakes and dams in the Philippines is used to produce kinetic energy to generate electricity for use in homes, communities, and industry
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about sound energy used for communication, not about potential energy in lakes/dams being converted to kinetic energy to generate electricity. No instructional support for this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: People use sound energy to communicate
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify examples of everyday situations that demonstrate: a. kinetic energy being transformed to potential energy, and b. potential energy being transformed to kinetic energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses sound energy and vocal cord vibration, not kinetic-to-potential or potential-to-kinetic energy transformations. It does not support this competency.

copy.en: People use sound energy to communicate - when we talk, sing, or shout, our vocal cords vibrate and send sound through the air to share information with others.
copy.tl: Ginagamit ng tao ang sound energy para makipag-usap - kapag nagsasalita, kumakanta, o sumisigaw tayo, nagva-vibrate ang ating vocal cords at nagpapadala ng tunog sa hangin para magbahagi ng impormasyon sa iba.
copy.bis: Gigamit sa mga tao ang sound energy aron makig-istorya - kung magsulti, mokanta, o mosinggit kita, mag-vibrate ang atong vocal cords ug magpadala og tingog sa hangin aron magpaambit og impormasyon sa uban.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sound travels as a longitudinal wave
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe living things, such as animals and plants, as biotic factors and light, water, temperature, and soil type, as abiotic factors in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes sound as a longitudinal/compression wave, a physics topic. G6-L-7 is about biotic and abiotic factors in an ecosystem, which is unrelated to sound waves.

copy.en: Sound travels as a longitudinal wave, also called a compression wave, because it moves by squeezing and stretching the medium it passes through.
copy.tl: Ang tunog ay naglalakbay bilang longitudinal wave, tinatawag ding compression wave, dahil gumagalaw ito sa pamamagitan ng pagsisiksik at pag-uunat sa medium na dinadaanan nito.
copy.bis: Ang tingog mobiyahe isip longitudinal wave, gitawag usab nga compression wave, tungod kay kini molihok pinaagi sa pagpislit ug pag-inat sa medium nga giagianan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sources of light include electric lights, sunlight, and candles
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how high voltage electricity from power plants is generated and safely distributed to industries, businesses, and homes, including the role of substations (grid stations), and electric meters
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes sources of light and reflection, which is unrelated to the competency about high voltage electricity generation and distribution from power plants, substations, and electric meters.

copy.en: Sources of light include electric lights, sunlight, and candles; some objects emit light while others can only be seen when light reflects from them.
copy.tl: Kabilang sa mga pinagmumulan ng liwanag ang electric lights, sikat ng araw, at kandila; ang ilang bagay ay naglalabas ng sariling liwanag habang ang iba ay nakikita lamang kapag tumalbog ang liwanag mula sa kanila.
copy.bis: Ang mga tinubdan sa kahayag naglakip sa electric lights, kahayag sa adlaw, ug kandila; ang uban nga mga butang nagpagawas og kaugalingong kahayag samtang ang uban makita lamang kung ang kahayag motalbog kanila.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water sources include ponds, rivers, seas, lakes, and deep wells
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes sources of water (ponds, rivers, seas, lakes, deep wells) and their daily uses. G6-M-4 requires describing useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures such as solutions and suspensions. The card contains no information about mixtures, solutions, or suspensions, so it does not support this competency at all.

copy.en: Water sources include ponds, rivers, seas, lakes, and deep wells, and each one gives us water for different daily activities.
copy.tl: Ang mga pinagkukunan ng tubig ay pond, ilog, dagat, lawa, at deep well, at bawat isa ay nagbibigay sa atin ng tubig para sa iba't ibang gawain araw-araw.
copy.bis: Ang mga tinubdan sa tubig naglakip sa pond, suba, dagat, lanaw, ug deep well, ug ang matag usa naghatag kanato ug tubig alang sa lain-laing buluhaton kada adlaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: their speed is 5 meters per second
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the advantage of high biodiversity in maintaining the stability of an ecosystem during difficult conditions, such as food shortages, disease, and climate change
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches speed calculation (distance/time), a physics/mathematics concept. G9-L-5 concerns biodiversity and ecosystem stability, which is unrelated to the card's content.

copy.en: If a football field is 100 meters long and a person runs its length in 20 seconds, their speed is 5 meters per second.
copy.tl: Kung ang football field ay 100 metro ang haba at tinakbo ito ng isang tao sa loob ng 20 segundo, ang speed niya ay 5 meters per second.
copy.bis: Kung ang football field 100 metros ang gitas-on ug gidagan kini sa usa ka tawo sa 20 segundos, ang iyang speed 5 meters per second.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Velocity tells you how fast an object is moving and in what direction
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Velocity as speed with direction is physics, not plant reproduction.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a car going 60 kilometers per hour heading north
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how interaction between living things and interactions between living and non-living things may bring good or harm to the living things involved
assignedReviews.reason: A car's velocity is not an interaction bringing good or harm to living things.

copy.en: Velocity tells you how fast an object is moving and in what direction, like a car going 60 kilometers per hour heading north.
copy.tl: Sinasabi ng velocity kung gaano kabilis gumagalaw ang isang bagay at sa anong direksyon, tulad ng kotse na tumatakbo ng 60 kilometers per hour papuntang hilaga.
copy.bis: Ang velocity nagsulti kanimo kung unsa kapaspas ang paglihok sa usa ka butang ug sa unsa nga direksyon, sama sa sakyanan nga nagdagan og 60 kilometers per hour paingon sa norte.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The sperm from the testes and the egg from the ovaries are the two sex cells
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use weather instruments to measure and record some of the characteristics of weather during a school day
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about gametes (sperm and egg), which is a biology topic. G4-E-5 requires using weather instruments to measure and record weather characteristics. There is no weather content or instrument use in the card.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The sperm from the testes and the egg from the ovaries are the two sex cells
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify some of the basic characteristics used to describe the weather, such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, wind direction, humidity, rain, and cloud cover
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about gametes, not about weather characteristics such as air temperature, air pressure, wind speed, etc. The card provides no instructional support for identifying weather characteristics.

copy.en: The sperm from the testes and the egg from the ovaries are the two sex cells, and together they are called gametes.
copy.tl: Ang sperm mula sa testes at ang egg mula sa ovaries ay ang dalawang sex cells, at magkasama silang tinatawag na gametes.
copy.bis: Ang sperm gikan sa testes ug ang egg gikan sa ovaries mao ang duha ka sex cells, ug kon magkauban kini gitawag ug gametes.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The epididymis is a coiled tube on the back of each testis where sperm cells are stored and gain the ability to move.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: discuss the factors that limit the ecosystem's carrying capacity, such as adequate food, shelter, water, and mates
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the epididymis, a male reproductive organ. G10-L-10 concerns ecosystem carrying capacity and limiting factors such as food, shelter, water, and mates. There is no connection to ecosystems or carrying capacity.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The epididymis is a coiled tube on the back of each testis where sperm cells are stored and gain the ability to move.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: G3-L-6 asks students to identify basic needs of all living things (air, food, water, shelter). The card is about sperm storage in the epididymis and does not address basic needs of living things.

copy.en: The epididymis is a coiled tube on the back of each testis where sperm cells are stored and gain the ability to move.
copy.tl: Ang epididymis ay isang nakapulupot na tubo sa likod ng bawat testis kung saan iniimbak ang sperm cells at nagkakaroon sila ng kakayahang gumalaw.
copy.bis: Ang epididymis usa ka naglikoliko nga tubo sa likod sa matag testis diin gitipigan ang sperm cells ug nakaangkon sila ug abilidad sa paglihok.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The initial velocity of a projectile
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: follow appropriate steps of a scientific investigation which includes: a. Aim or problem, b. Materials and equipment, c. Method or procedures, d. Results including data, and e. Conclusion
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains splitting projectile velocity into horizontal and vertical components, which is a physics concept (projectile motion). It does not address the steps of a scientific investigation (aim, materials, method, results, conclusion) at all.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The initial velocity of a projectile
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize the features of a fair test and that scientific investigations also involve doing at least three trials, or use replication, and observing, measuring, and recording accurately
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about projectile motion components, not about fair test features, replication, or accurate measurement in scientific investigations. No connection to the competency's content.

copy.en: The initial velocity of a projectile can be split into a horizontal component and a vertical component, which are analyzed separately.
copy.tl: Ang initial velocity ng isang projectile ay maaaring hatiin sa horizontal component at vertical component, na sinusuri nang magkahiwalay.
copy.bis: Ang initial velocity sa usa ka projectile mahimong bahinon ngadto sa horizontal component ug vertical component, nga analisahon nga gilain.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In spring, the weather gets warmer and sunnier, trees and plants start to grow, and many animals have their babies!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and describe some of the materials formed during volcanic eruptions in the Philippines
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes seasonal changes in spring (weather, plant growth, animal births). The competency G6-E-4 requires identifying and describing materials formed during volcanic eruptions in the Philippines. There is no connection to volcanic materials or eruptions.

copy.en:
What happens in spring?

In spring, the weather gets warmer and sunnier, trees and plants start to grow, and many animals have their babies!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari sa spring?

Sa spring, umiinit at sumisikat ang panahon, nagsisimulang tumubo ang mga puno at halaman, at maraming hayop ang nanganganak!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang mahitabo sa spring?

Sa spring, moinit ug mosidlak ang panahon, magsugod pagtubo ang mga kahoy ug tanom, ug daghang mananap ang manganak!
